hosting.comment: measure-pressure-app.web.app - the app, the clinician view, and the API. This is the address saved to a home screen, so it does not move.

rewrites.comment: The API. Rewritten rather than called cross-origin, so the browser sees one origin and the session cookie works with no CORS involved.
The clinician app routes on the client; any /doctor path without a file falls back to its own index.
Everything else belongs to the patient app.

headers.comment: Applies to every path, including '/' and the clean URLs, which a *.html glob would miss because these rules match the request path rather than the file served. Medical pages, so keep them out of caches and referrers.
Listed after the catch-all so it wins: fingerprinted bundles never change under the same name, so they can be cached forever.
Listed last so it wins over the catch-all: API responses carry medical data and must not be written to any cache, not merely revalidated.

hosting.comment: measurepressure.web.app - the landing page, on its own origin. Deliberately not a path on the app's site: a separate origin keeps the session cookie and the installed app's scope away from a public page, and means a link to it opens in the browser rather than inside the home-screen app.

rewrites.comment: One page. Anything that is not a file gets it.

headers.comment: No medical data here, so this can be cached - but only briefly, so a correction to the install instructions reaches a phone that has already been sent the link.
Listed last so it wins: the bundles are fingerprinted, so they never change under the same name.
